chunks: We shall cast out any grudge they may have in their hearts. (There) they will sit on couches face to face like brothers together.

key_terms.غِلٍّ: Grudge or envy in the heart

ai.seo_question: What happens to the hearts of believers in Paradise regarding envy and grudges?
ai.summary: In Shia exegesis, the removal of 'ghill' (inner malice) signifies the purification of the heart through divine grace, reflecting the ultimate state of 'ikhwa' (brotherhood) rooted in shared love for the Ahl al-Bayt. The imagery of sitting on 'surur mutaqabilin' (couches facing each other) emphasizes not only physical comfort but also the spiritual intimacy and equality of the believers in the presence of God. This verse is often cited to illustrate the transition from the worldly state of competition to the eternal state of harmonious communion.
